h.strategy: Propose hypotheses where the condition plausibly changes the edit's effect by a large amount through a simple mechanism: redundancy (an alternative path or component already provides what the edit adds), disconnection (the edited part cannot influence the outcome under the condition), saturation (gains shrink when capacity is already high), or bottleneck (gains grow when the edited part is the limiting factor). Make sure the direction follows unambiguously from the mechanism. Avoid conditions unrelated to the edited part.

hyps.why: With one parallel route to the output removed, the direct residual path carries more of the benefit.
Adding a skip where nothing existed gains more than replacing an existing op, which gives up its learned features.
A pooling partner on the serial path bottlenecks and blurs the features, so the conv upgrade gains less.
A strong alternative route into node 2 makes edge 2 redundant, so removing it costs less.
With edge 5 gone, removing the direct edge leaves only the single serial path 0→1→3, so the loss is larger.
Replacing a conv with a parameter-free pool throws away learnable capacity, unlike pooling in place of skip or none.
A direct residual path already exists, so a second skip via node 1 is redundant.
Adding a conv on the direct edge where none existed gains more than swapping out an existing skip or pool.
Activating the node 2 to output edge with a conv adds a whole path, a larger gain than upgrading an op already there.
With the direct edge absent, removing edge 4 leaves only the route through node 2, so the loss is larger.
